I was always the type to overcomplicate things. So when I accidentally left my laptop charger at home and had to borrow one from a colleague, I felt mortified. I walked into the office, tail between my legs, clutching the borrowed charger like a trophy.

That day, I realized my tendency to overthink and overreact was holding me back. I was letting one minor mistake define my whole day. My colleague, noticing my distress, took me aside. She explained that everyone makes mistakes - it's how we learn and move forward.

That conversation made me reflect. I began to let go of the small things and focus on the bigger picture. Instead of dwelling on my perceived slip-up, I used it as a teachable moment. I learned the importance of not making a mountain out of a molehill. That one small misstep taught me a valuable life lesson about perspective and resilience.

In the end, I was grateful for that simple borrowing of a charger. It served as a reminder to approach life with a more balanced and forgiving mindset. Sometimes, our greatest lessons come from our smallest mistakes.
